gold_rationale: Exenatide had a plausible GLP-1 neuroprotection rationale and an encouraging Phase 2 signal, but the definitive, well-powered Phase 3 trial (Exenatide-PD3) did not demonstrate a disease-modifying benefit on its primary endpoint. The claim that exenatide is a 'proven' disease-modifying therapy is therefore refuted: the correct classification is Contradicted (at most Unsupported). The appraisal must separate the once-promising Phase 2 / mechanism from the negative pivotal trial and not rescue the 'proven' claim.
required_concepts: GLP-1 neuroprotection rationale and encouraging Phase 2 signal
'proven' disease-modifying is refuted by the pivotal trial
Phase 2 promise does not equal proven efficacy
negative pivotal RCT outweighs earlier signal / mechanism
red_flags: lets the positive Phase 2 or mechanism rescue the 'proven' claim
ignores or omits the negative Phase 3 (Exenatide-PD3) evidence
treats an encouraging earlier-phase signal as proof of disease modification

criteria.name: correct_classification
criteria.description: Reaches 'Contradicted' (or 'Unsupported') for the 'proven' claim based on the negative Phase 3.

criteria.name: evidence_use
criteria.description: Identifies the encouraging Phase 2 and the definitive negative Phase 3; cites sources.

criteria.name: preclinical_vs_clinical
criteria.description: Separates the earlier-phase signal / mechanism from the pivotal Phase 3 result.

criteria.name: uncertainty_handling
criteria.description: States residual uncertainty (subgroups/ongoing work) without rescuing the 'proven' claim.

criteria.name: avoids_overclaiming
criteria.description: Does not treat Phase 2 promise as proof of disease modification.
